## MICRO-MISSION 60-B — SOCIAL AUTOMATION BATCH B

**Status: BATCH B COMPLETE (4/4 platforms).** Batch A (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok) was not returned to except where a shared regression required verification (X's retry/idempotency retrofit touches the shared `socialPublishSupport.cjs`/`oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs` files Batch A also depends on — re-verified below, no regressions found).

### X

**Implementation:** Existing adapter (`backend/services/socialPostingService.cjs`) preserved, not rewritten. M59 flagged it as having no retry/backoff or idempotency (P2 GAP) and no `.env.example` template (fixed in Batch A). This mission closed the retry/idempotency gap by wiring in the same `socialPublishSupport.cjs` helper every Batch A adapter already uses — every existing line of behavior (honest not-configured failure, 280-char limit, `DISABLE_SOCIAL_POSTING` kill-switch, org-scoped vault-then-env token resolution) is unchanged; only the network call is now retry-wrapped and a new optional 3rd `idempotencyKey` parameter was added (default `null`, fully backward compatible).
**Credential requirements:** `TWITTER_BEARER_TOKEN`/`X_BEARER_TOKEN` (unchanged from M59/Batch A — still absent from `.env` at time of writing, template already added to `.env.example` in Batch A).
**Runtime configuration:** Vault-first (`social:twitter`/`oauth_token`, org-scoped) then global env fallback — unchanged.
**Authentication:** Single bearer token — unchanged, no OAuth flow exists or is needed for X's API v2 posting model.
**Publishing:** Text only, 280-char limit — unchanged.
**Scheduler/Queue:** None (immediate-publish, per this mission's scope decision) — unchanged from Batch A's architecture decision; now has retry/backoff for transient failures.
**Security:** Unchanged — same `attachOrg` + `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext` gate from the org-IDOR fix (test 114), re-verified passing.
**Error/Rate Limit:** Real HTTP status/detail passthrough — unchanged; now additionally retries 429/5xx transiently before surfacing a final error.
**Tests:** `tests/security/132-x-social-publish-retry-idempotency.cjs` (new) — 16/16 pass, explicitly verifying every pre-existing behavior is unchanged AND the new retry/idempotency wiring works; `tests/security/114-...cjs`/`66-...cjs` (pre-existing, re-run) — 11/3 pass, no regression.
**Status:** IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (retrofit), CREDENTIAL-BLOCKED (no token configured) — no external app-review gate for this scope.

### Threads

**Implementation:** From-scratch adapter, `backend/services/threadsPostingService.cjs`. No prior Threads code existed beyond content-generation spec text (platform metadata only). Threads has its own Meta developer app and OAuth flow (`threads.net`), genuinely distinct from Instagram/Facebook's Graph API despite being a Meta product — added as its own `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs` provider entry, not folded into `facebook`. Real two-step Threads Publishing API (`POST /{threads-user-id}/threads` → `POST /{threads-user-id}/threads_publish`), same container-then-publish shape as Instagram's — a genuine Meta API-family convention.
**Credential requirements:** `THREADS_CLIENT_ID`, `THREADS_CLIENT_SECRET`, `THREADS_REDIRECT_URI` — all new, none set.
**Runtime configuration:** Vault-first (`social:threads`) then OAuth connection fallback — same pattern as every other adapter.
**Authentication:** OAuth2, `threads_basic`/`threads_content_publish` scopes.
**Publishing:** Text (up to 500 chars, Threads' real limit) — genuinely supported with NO public media URL required, unlike Instagram. Image/video also supported when a public `https://` `mediaUrl` + explicit `mediaType` is supplied.
**Scheduler/Queue:** None (immediate-publish, per mission scope decision).
**Security:** Same `attachOrg` + `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext` gate.
**Error/Rate Limit:** Real HTTP status/detail passthrough; retry on the container-creation step only (publish step not auto-retried, to avoid a duplicate post from an ambiguous network timeout after a container is already created).
**Tests:** `tests/security/133-threads-social-publish-isolation.cjs` — 20/20 pass (route wiring + gate, honest failure, text-only-post validation-path confirmation, mediaType/mediaUrl contract enforcement, 500-char limit).
**Status:** IMPLEMENTED, CREDENTIAL-BLOCKED. External blocker: `threads_content_publish` requires Meta App Review (same category as Facebook/Instagram's Advanced Access gate).

### Pinterest

**Implementation:** From-scratch adapter, `backend/services/pinterestPostingService.cjs`. No prior Pinterest code existed at all. Pinterest's real Pin creation is a SINGLE-CALL API (`POST /v5/pins`) — unlike the two-step container flows of Instagram/Threads/YouTube/TikTok, closer in shape to X/LinkedIn. Also added `GET /creative/social/publish/pinterest/boards` since Pinterest has no "default board" concept — a caller must choose a `board_id`.
**Credential requirements:** `PINTEREST_APP_ID`, `PINTEREST_APP_SECRET`, `PINTEREST_REDIRECT_URI` — all new, none set.
**Runtime configuration:** Vault-first (`social:pinterest`) then OAuth connection fallback.
**Authentication:** OAuth2 with Basic-auth token exchange (client credentials in the Authorization header, not the body) — required a genuine generalization of `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs`'s token-exchange code, previously hardcoded to `provider === "notion"`. Generalized to a `tokenAuthMode: "basic"` config field, with Notion's specific JSON-body requirement kept as an explicit documented exception inside that branch (Notion wants a JSON body even with Basic auth; every other Basic-auth provider, including Pinterest, wants the same form-encoded body as non-Basic providers). **A real regression was caught and fixed during this generalization**: the branch condition changed from `provider === "notion"` to `cfg.tokenAuthMode === "basic"`, which required also adding `tokenAuthMode: "basic"` to Notion's own config — missing that would have silently broken Notion's OAuth callback. Caught by manual verification before shipping, then locked in by a dedicated regression test.
**Publishing:** Image pins with title/description/link — Pinterest's real fields; no pure-text pin type exists (a real provider constraint, not an omission).
**Scheduler/Queue:** None (immediate-publish, per mission scope decision).
**Security:** Same `attachOrg` + `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext` gate, applied to all three new routes (boards list, create, delete).
**Error/Rate Limit:** Real HTTP status/detail passthrough; retry-wrapped (single-call submit is safely retryable end-to-end, unlike the two-step flows).
**Tests:** `tests/security/134-pinterest-social-publish-isolation.cjs` — 25/25 pass, including an explicit Notion-regression check verifying the pre-existing Basic-auth provider still works identically after the `tokenAuthMode` generalization.
**Status:** IMPLEMENTED, CREDENTIAL-BLOCKED — no external app-review gate found for this scope at time of writing (Pinterest's standard API access does not require the kind of Advanced-Access review Meta/TikTok/Google impose).

### Reddit

**Implementation:** From-scratch adapter, `backend/services/redditPostingService.cjs`. The existing `agents/internet/socialMediaAgent.cjs` is explicitly documented as read-only (public, unauthenticated Reddit/HN JSON endpoints only) and was left completely untouched — verified via `git diff --stat` showing zero changes to that file. This is a genuinely new, separate submit capability, not a rewrite. Real `POST /api/submit` endpoint, `kind=self` (text) or `kind=link` (URL), with the Reddit-required descriptive `User-Agent` header (built from the real configured `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID`, not a hardcoded placeholder).
**Credential requirements:** `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID`, `REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET`, `REDDIT_REDIRECT_URI` — all new, none set.
**Runtime configuration:** Vault-first (`social:reddit`) then OAuth connection fallback.
**Authentication:** OAuth2, "web app" type (not "script" — a real user-facing connect flow), Basic-auth token exchange (reused the same `tokenAuthMode: "basic"` generalization Pinterest required — no new special-casing needed), `duration=permanent` requested so a real refresh token is issued (without it, Reddit issues only a 1-hour token with no refresh capability at all).
**Publishing:** Self (text) or link posts, up to 300 chars title (Reddit's real limit). Image/video native upload is explicitly OUT of scope this mission — Reddit's media submission is a separate multi-step lease/upload/websocket-confirmation flow, a genuinely larger feature than "smallest adapter" calls for; a link post pointing at an already-hosted image works today.
**Scheduler/Queue:** None (immediate-publish, per mission scope decision).
**Security:** Same `attachOrg` + `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext` gate.
**Error/Rate Limit:** Real Reddit API error array parsed and surfaced (`json.errors`), plus real HTTP status/detail; retry-wrapped (single-call submit).
**Tests:** `tests/security/135-reddit-social-publish-isolation.cjs` — 21/21 pass, including an explicit check that the pre-existing read-only agent's docstring and capability set are unchanged.
**Status:** IMPLEMENTED, CREDENTIAL-BLOCKED — no external app-review gate found for this scope (Reddit's standard OAuth app creation is self-service, no formal review process like Meta/TikTok/Google impose for their equivalent scopes).

## MICRO-MISSION 60-C — SOCIAL AUTOMATION BATCH C

**Status: BATCH C COMPLETE (4/4 platforms addressed). This is the FINAL social implementation batch — all 13 platforms across Batch A/B/C have now been addressed** (built, retrofitted, wired to an existing capability, or explicitly documented as out of scope with reasoning, per what each platform's real provider API and this repo's existing architecture actually support).

### Discord

**Implementation:** From-scratch adapter, `backend/services/discordPostingService.cjs`. M59 found only OAuth-identity/reachability probes (`connectDiscord`/`connectDiscordAuth` in `integrationConnectors.cjs`) — never a message-send path. Discord is registered under this repo's "msg" (messaging) connector phase, alongside WhatsApp/Telegram/Twilio/Slack/Teams — consistent with treating it as a community/messaging channel rather than a feed-style social network. "Post a message to a channel" is still a real, in-scope publishing capability (text content reaching an audience via a provider API, the same definition every other adapter uses), so it was implemented rather than left identity-only. Two independent real send paths, whichever credential is configured: webhook (`DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`, single POST, no bot-gateway needed) or bot REST API (`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` + an explicit `channelId`, `POST /channels/{id}/messages`).
**Authentication:** Bot token (`Bot <token>` header) or webhook URL — no new OAuth needed; reuses the existing `msg:discord` connectorId `integrationConnectors.cjs` already probes.
**Credentials:** `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and/or `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` — both already templated in `.env.example` since before this mission; no new env vars added. `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` key exists but is empty; `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` key is absent.
**Publishing:** Text only, 2000-char limit (Discord's real message length limit).
**Scheduler/Queue:** None (immediate-publish, per this mission's Batch A scope decision, applies consistently here).
**Security:** Same `attachOrg` + `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext` gate as every other platform.
**Error/Rate Limit:** Real HTTP status/detail passthrough; retry-wrapped (single-call send, safely retryable).
**Tests:** `tests/security/136-discord-social-publish-isolation.cjs` — 19/19 pass (route wiring + gate, honest failure, dual-path channelId requirement, 2000-char limit, kill-switch, `myConnectors.js` connectorId reuse verification).
**Runtime:** No live credential configured — not runtime-verified.
**Status:** IMPLEMENTED, CREDENTIAL-BLOCKED. No external app-review gate found for this scope.

### Telegram

**Existing Capability:** Already LIVE VERIFIED (M53, re-confirmed live by M59's `getMe` call). `telegramService.js`'s `sendMessage(chatId, text)` already does exactly what social publishing needs — a real HTTP call to any `chatId`, which can be a public channel's `@handle` the bot administers, not just an operator DM. `backend/routes/telegram.js` already exposes `POST /telegram/send` (auth-gated, global-token, no org scoping, no idempotency/retry, not tied into the social content-generation flow).
**Social Publishing Capability:** The underlying send capability already existed and needed no new code — what was genuinely missing was orchestration wiring: a `/creative/social/publish/telegram` route bringing the existing, unmodified `sendMessage()` into Module 7's same idempotency/retry/org-gate conventions as every other platform, so a generated caption can reach a real channel through the same flow as every other platform. `telegramService.js` and `backend/routes/telegram.js` were NOT modified — verified via `git diff --stat` showing zero changes to either file.
**Credentials:** `TELEGRAM_TOKEN` — unchanged, already present and non-empty (live-verified in M59; not re-called externally this mission per the mission's explicit "do not repeat unnecessarily" instruction).
**Scheduler/Queue:** None (immediate-publish).
**Security:** New route gated by `attachOrg` + `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext`, same as every other platform; a genuine fix was needed at the call site — `sendMessage()` returns `{sent, reason, status}`, not `socialPublishSupport.withRetry()`'s expected `{success, status}` shape. Adapted the shape at the route's call site only (never modifying `telegramService.js`) so a real send is never misread as a failure and needlessly retried.
**Tests:** `tests/security/137-telegram-social-publish-wiring.cjs` — 15/15 pass, including explicit `git diff --stat` assertions proving `telegramService.js`/`telegram.js` are byte-for-byte unmodified, and a check that `telegramService.js`'s exports are unchanged (still exactly `sendMessage`/`isConfigured`, nothing added).
**Runtime:** Already live-verified by M59; not re-validated this mission (per instruction).
**Status:** LIVE-VERIFIED CAPABILITY, NEWLY WIRED into social orchestration. Existing bot identity/messaging/CRM behavior fully preserved.

### WhatsApp

**Existing Capability:** Already LIVE VERIFIED (M53, re-confirmed live by M59's phone-metadata GET). `whatsappService.js`'s `sendMessage(phone, text, retries, orgId)` is real, org-scoped, hardened (webhook HMAC verification, replay protection, auth cooldown) — but is explicitly 1:1 and capped-bulk messaging to individual phone numbers (`backend/routes/whatsapp.js`'s `/whatsapp/send` and `/whatsapp/bulk`).
**Social Publishing Capability: genuinely does not exist, and was not manufactured.** The WhatsApp Business Cloud API (the API this integration uses) has NO channel/feed/broadcast publish primitive at all — confirmed by re-inspecting `whatsappService.js` for any status/broadcast/template capability (none exists). WhatsApp's very limited "Status" broadcast feature belongs to the separate WhatsApp Business *app*, not the Cloud API, and is not reachable through this integration regardless. Forcing a `/creative/social/publish/whatsapp` route would mean either sending to one individual's phone number (not social publishing in any real sense — the existing `/whatsapp/bulk` CRM route already covers that use case) or fabricating a capability the provider does not expose — both explicitly forbidden by this mission's "do NOT manufacture a social publishing capability" instruction.
**Credentials:** `WA_TOKEN`, `WA_PHONE_ID` — unchanged, already present and non-empty (live-verified in M59; not re-called externally this mission).
**Scheduler/Queue:** N/A — no new route added.
**Security:** Unchanged — existing org-scoped vault resolution, webhook HMAC verification, and auth cooldown all untouched.
**Tests:** None added — no code was changed. (`git diff --stat -- backend/services/whatsappService.js backend/routes/whatsapp.js` confirms zero changes.)
**Runtime:** Already live-verified by M59; not re-validated this mission.
**Status:** LIVE-VERIFIED, EXISTING BUSINESS-MESSAGING CHANNEL — explicitly documented as OUT OF SOCIAL-PUBLISHING SCOPE, not a gap. WhatsApp remains a real, working, production-grade CRM/lead-messaging channel for its actual purpose; it is not, and cannot become without a fundamentally different product/API, a social content distribution channel.

### Google Business Profile

**Implementation:** From-scratch adapter, `backend/services/gbpPostingService.cjs` (the 13th and final platform). No prior code of any kind existed — confirmed absent from `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs` and `integrationConnectors.cjs`. Real Business Profile Local Posts API, requiring genuine account/location resolution before a post can target a specific location (no "default location" concept in this provider's model): `GET .../accounts` (list Business accounts) → `GET .../accounts/{id}/locations` (list locations under one account) → `POST .../locations/{id}/localPosts` (create the post). The Local Posts creation call itself remains on the legacy `mybusiness.googleapis.com/v4` host — Google split account/location management into newer APIs but did not migrate Local Posts creation at time of writing; the real, currently-documented endpoint was used, not a guessed one.
**Authentication:** New `gbp` OAuth provider entry in `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs` — deliberately separate from the existing shared `google`/`youtube` entries (same reasoning as Facebook-vs-WhatsApp and YouTube-vs-Google: a dedicated `business.manage` scope should not silently ride an existing Gmail/Drive/YouTube connection or force an unwanted re-consent on it).
**Credentials:** `GBP_CLIENT_ID`, `GBP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GBP_REDIRECT_URI` — all new, both absent from `.env` (falls back to `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`SECRET` if a dedicated app isn't configured, same pattern as YouTube).
**Publishing:** Text summary post (max 1500 chars, Google Business Profile's real limit) with an optional call-to-action link.
**Media:** Not implemented this pass — Local Posts supports an optional image, but doing so correctly requires the same "publicly-fetchable media URL" constraint already documented for Instagram/Threads/Pinterest; deferred consistent with this mission's per-platform scoping (text-first, media as a documented follow-up where the pattern is already established elsewhere).
**Scheduler/Queue:** None (immediate-publish).
**Security:** Same `attachOrg` + `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext` gate, applied to all three new routes (accounts list, locations list, post create).
**Error/Rate Limit:** Real HTTP status/detail passthrough; retry-wrapped (single-call create, safely retryable).
**Tests:** `tests/security/138-gbp-social-publish-isolation.cjs` — 20/20 pass after one real bug was caught and fixed during test-writing: `listLocations()` checked the token before checking whether `accountName` was even supplied, so an unconfigured environment returned "not configured" instead of the more useful "accountName required" validation error — reordered to validate input shape first, consistent with every other adapter's own check ordering (`createPost` in the same file already validates `locationName`/`summary` before checking credentials).
**Runtime:** No live credential configured — not runtime-verified.
**Status:** IMPLEMENTED, CREDENTIAL-BLOCKED. External blocker: the Business Profile Performance/Posts APIs are NOT self-service — Google requires a manual API-access request (a form + review, historically days-to-weeks) before a Cloud project can call them at all, even in testing. This is stricter than YouTube's upload-scope verification and a genuinely distinct, separate external gate.

## GOOGLE ECOSYSTEM — IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETION

**Scope decision (made before implementation):** A repo-wide discovery pass across all 31 named Google/Firebase categories found real, in-scope, buildable gaps in exactly 3 places — Gmail, Google Drive (both had real OAuth scopes already requested and a real tool definition already pointing at the correct `googleapis.com` base URL, but an explicit `not_configured` stub instead of a real call), and FCM push send (real token registration/storage/readiness already existed; `send()` was an honestly-labeled stub with a comment literally saying "FCM send path not yet implemented"). Google Calendar, Docs, and Meet are genuinely config-presence-only probes (no scope requested, no workflow depends on them today) and were left unbuilt, consistent with this mission's own rule against inventing unrelated scope. 12 of the 31 categories (Ads, Search Console, Maps, Places, Geocoding, Routes/Directions, Contacts, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, Merchant Center, Vertex AI, Cloud Storage) have **zero** prior reference anywhere in the repo — building any of them would be inventing new scope this mission explicitly forbids, so none were touched.

### CODE-COMPLETE

- **Gmail** — send/read/search/reply, real `gmail.googleapis.com` calls, existing `execute()` pipeline (permission/rate-limit/retry/usage-logging) unchanged.
- **Google Drive** — list/download/upload(metadata)/delete, real `googleapis.com/drive/v3` calls, same pipeline.
- **FCM push send** — real `firebase-admin` `messaging().send()` per token, stale-token pruning, per-token error isolation.
- (Pre-existing, confirmed unchanged this mission, already CODE-COMPLETE from prior missions): Google Business Profile, YouTube.

### PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED

- **Google OAuth / Identity** — the connection/token layer is real and complete, but 2 of the 3 scopes it already requests (`gmail.readonly`, `drive.readonly`) were dead until this mission; now genuinely redeemed by Gmail/Drive. (Note: Gmail's `send_email`/`reply_email` actions need write scopes broader than the currently-requested `gmail.readonly` — see New Blockers.)
- **Firebase (server, general)** — `connectFirebase()`'s local JSON-parse-only check is unchanged; this mission built real FCM send on top of it without altering that readiness check itself.

### BUILT THIS MISSION

1. `backend/services/toolExecutionLayer.cjs` — added `_googleToken(userId)` helper (resolves a Google OAuth token via the existing `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs`, `"founder"` default per `founderVault.js`'s established single-tenant convention); replaced the `gmail`/`gdrive` stub cases with real `gmail.googleapis.com`/`googleapis.com/drive/v3` HTTP calls; threaded `opts` into `_runAdapter()` so per-call `userId` can reach the new helper (backward compatible — the one existing caller, `backend/routes/phase19.js`, is unaffected since it never passed `userId` before either).
2. `backend/services/pushNotificationEngine.cjs` — added `_firebaseAdmin()` (optional-require, same pattern as `backend/routes/auth.js`'s `_firebaseAdmin()`) and `_initFirebaseApp()` (initializes the Admin SDK once per process from the existing `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` JSON `connectFirebase()` already parses); replaced `send()`'s stub with a real per-token `messaging().send()` loop, stale-token detection/pruning (`messaging/registration-token-not-registered`), and truncated-token error records (never the full token).

### STILL MISSING

- **Gmail write scopes**: `send_email`/`reply_email` will fail with a real permissions error once a Google OAuth connection exists, because the `google` provider's `defaultScopes` in `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs` only include `gmail.readonly` — sending requires `gmail.send` or `gmail.modify`. This is flagged, not silently left broken; adding the scope is a one-line change but was **not** made this mission since it would force a re-consent on any existing Google connection and this mission's scope was "wire the existing stub to reality," not "expand scopes speculatively" — recommend doing this explicitly in the credential-provisioning phase, alongside deciding whether write access is actually wanted.
- **Google Drive full file upload**: only metadata-only file creation is implemented (a real Drive file record is created, but no actual byte content is attached) — full resumable multipart upload with real bytes is a genuinely larger feature, deferred consistent with the "smallest adapter" scoping used throughout this mission's social batches. Documented in the adapter's own code comment, not silently dropped.
- **Google Calendar / Docs / Meet real API paths** — correctly left unbuilt (config-probe only), since no existing workflow currently depends on them and building them would exceed this mission's "only genuinely in-scope" rule.

### OUT OF SCOPE

Google Ads, Search Console, Maps, Places, Geocoding, Routes/Directions, Contacts, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, Merchant Center, Google Cloud (GCP)/Cloud Storage, Vertex AI, Google Play/Android distribution automation — all confirmed to have zero prior reference anywhere in the repo (or, for GCP, only a provider-name label with no SDK/API usage). Building any of these would be inventing new scope this mission explicitly forbids.

### PROVIDER APPROVAL REQUIRED LATER

- **Gmail send/modify scopes**: Google classifies `gmail.send`/`gmail.modify` as "Restricted" scopes requiring a security assessment (CASA/annual review) for verified apps requesting them from external users — distinct from and more involved than the general OAuth verification already noted for YouTube/GBP in prior missions.
- **Google Drive write scopes**: similarly sensitive-scope territory once `drive.file`/`drive` is requested instead of read-only.
- **FCM**: no provider-side approval process — purely a credential/dependency provisioning matter.

### NEW BLOCKERS

Only genuinely new findings this mission:
1. **`firebase-admin` is referenced in code (`auth.js`) but is not an installed dependency** — confirmed by direct `node_modules` inspection, not assumed. This silently degrades Firebase ID-token verification to a dev-only warning in every environment today (the `admin.apps?.length` check can never be true if the package was never even required successfully, or if `initializeApp()` is never called — which it currently isn't, anywhere, including in `auth.js` itself). This is pre-existing and outside this mission's scope to fix (installing a new npm dependency is a decision beyond "wire existing stub"), but is flagged here since it also blocks FCM's real send from ever succeeding until resolved.
2. **Gmail's currently-requested scope (`gmail.readonly`) cannot support the send/reply actions this mission just wired** — a real, working HTTP call exists for `send_email`/`reply_email`, but it will always receive a real 403 from Google until the scope is widened. Flagged explicitly rather than silently shipping a capability that can never succeed.
3. **`toolExecutionLayer.js`'s only existing caller (`backend/routes/phase19.js`) has no `attachOrg`/tenant-scoping middleware at all** — this is a pre-existing condition (confirmed: this legacy `/p19/*` route family predates the org-scoping pattern established elsewhere and was not touched by this mission), not a regression introduced here. Flagged for awareness since it means Gmail/Drive, once credentialed, would currently only ever resolve the single `"founder"` identity through this specific route — consistent with every other tool in `toolExecutionLayer.cjs` today, not a new gap this mission created.

### TESTS EXECUTED

Only focused tests, no full corpus:
- `tests/security/139-gmail-gdrive-tool-execution-real-api.cjs` (new) — 14/14 pass. Notably one test made a real network call to `gmail.googleapis.com` with a deliberately invalid token and received a genuine 401 rejection from Google's real API — proof the wiring reaches the real endpoint, not a mock, while remaining completely safe (no real account exists behind the fake token).
- `tests/security/140-fcm-push-send-real-api.cjs` (new) — 17/17 pass, using an injected fake `firebase-admin` module (via `require.cache`/`Module._load` override, no real dependency needed) to verify the real send-loop logic (per-token isolation, stale-token pruning, truncated error tokens) without any real network call.

### LIVE API CALLS

One incidental real call occurred as a direct, unavoidable consequence of testing the honest-failure path: `139-...cjs`'s "Unsupported action returns a real error" test passed a deliberately fake bearer token to `gmail.googleapis.com`'s real `messages` endpoint and received a real HTTP 401 (`invalid authentication credentials`) — this is a real API call, but it carried no real credential and could not have succeeded or caused any effect regardless of the fake token supplied. No other live call was made to any Google/Firebase API this mission (the FCM test used a fully injected fake SDK with zero network access).

### PUBLIC SIDE EFFECTS

NONE. No email sent, no file created/deleted, no push notification delivered to a real device, no calendar/doc/task/account modified anywhere.

### CREDENTIAL VALUES EXPOSED

NO. No credential value was read, printed, or logged. `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`'s test values used above were synthetic, fabricated strings for test isolation only (`"private_key":"fake"`), never a real credential.

### PRODUCTION CODE CHANGES

- `backend/services/toolExecutionLayer.cjs` — Gmail/Drive real API wiring (106 lines changed).
- `backend/services/pushNotificationEngine.cjs` — real FCM send implementation (119 lines changed).

### DATA CHANGES

NONE persisted. `data/push-tokens.json` was written to and cleaned up during test execution (confirmed empty `{"tokens":[]}` after the test run) — no residual data left behind.

## AI ECOSYSTEM — IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETION

**Scope decision (made before implementation):** A full discovery pass over `backend/services/aiService.js` (1358 lines, the central AI provider router) found **all 14 providers already genuinely implemented** — real HTTP calls to correct real API base URLs, real per-provider health checks, real per-provider timeouts, and a working sequential-fallback + retry layer. This is a mature subsystem, not a greenfield build. Discovery surfaced 3 additive, low-risk, well-grounded gaps that were built this mission (tool-calling extended to 5 more genuinely-compatible providers; LM Studio added to streaming), and several genuinely larger gaps (real token/cost accounting, embeddings, vision, secretVault integration for AI keys, unifying the two parallel call paths) that were deliberately **not** touched, since fixing them properly would mean changing the return-value contract of all 14 adapter functions or otherwise redesigning shared architecture — explicitly forbidden by this mission's "do not redesign" rule. Those are reported as genuine, precisely-scoped findings for a future mission, not silently dropped.

### BUILT THIS MISSION

1. **`chatWithTools()` extended from 4 to 9 tool-capable providers** — added `groq`, `deepseek`, `together`, `fireworks`, `nvidia` to `TOOL_CAPABLE`, each wired to the existing, already-shared `_openaiCompatWithTools(url, key, messages, tools, model, defaultModel, timeout, opts)` helper using constants (`GROQ_URL`, `_deepseekModel()`, etc.) that already existed and were already used for these providers' streaming/chat adapters — zero new parsing logic, purely additive wiring. `cohere`/`qwen`/`grok`/`ollama`/`lmstudio` deliberately left out (unverified against each provider's real tools request shape in this codebase — recorded as PROVIDER-LIMITATION per Task 4, not silently guessed at).

## PAYMENTS ECOSYSTEM — IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETION

**Scope decision (made before implementation):** A discovery pass across all 5 named providers found Razorpay is the sole real, working payment gateway in this repo (real SDK, real payment links, real subscriptions, real webhook HMAC verification, org-scoped credential resolution) — Stripe/PayPal/Paddle/Lemon Squeezy have zero executable code beyond credential-health probes, confirmed by this repo's own prior audit (`reports/OOPLIX-V1-MASTER-AUDIT-REGISTER.md`: "No Stripe or PayPal implementation exists — confirmed via full-repo search"). Direct verification (not just the discovery agent's summary) confirmed two genuine, precisely-scoped, high-value gaps in Razorpay's existing implementation: (1) `/payment/link` never mounted `attachOrg`, so the org-scoped credential resolution `paymentService.js` already had was structurally unreachable — the route's own prior comment predicted exactly this ("this only activates once org context is attached"); (2) refunds never reached Razorpay's real gateway API at all — only an internal credit-note record existed, even though `parseWebhookEvent()` already parsed real `refund.processed` events nothing ever produced. Both were built this mission, reusing existing security infrastructure exactly (the same `attachOrg`+membership-gate pattern proven across all 13 social platforms; the same `wf_refund_finance` HIGH-risk, never-auto-approved approval policy already gating the internal credit-note refund path). Building Stripe/PayPal/Paddle/LemonSqueezy from scratch was explicitly out of scope per this mission's own rule — the vault/env/probe plumbing exists for all 4, but no executable code exists to extend, and building a full payment gateway integration from zero is a fundamentally larger initiative than closing an existing, self-documented gap.

### CODE-COMPLETE

### BUILT THIS MISSION

1. **`backend/routes/payment.js` — tenant-scoping fix on `/payment/link`.** Mounted `attachOrg` + a new `_requireOrgMemberIfOrgContext` gate (identical pattern to the one proven across all 13 social platforms and the org-IDOR fix in test 114) before the existing handler. `attachOrg` alone is non-blocking (resolves `req.org` from a caller-supplied `X-Org-Id`/`body.orgId` with no membership check, per `orgMiddleware.cjs`'s own docstring) — mounting it without a follow-up gate would have been a new cross-tenant credential-hijack, not a fix, so both were added together. A solo caller with no org at all still falls through to the documented global Razorpay/WhatsApp env fallback, completely unaffected.
2. **`backend/services/paymentService.js` — real gateway refund.** Added `refundPayment(paymentId, {amount, orgId, idempotencyKey})`, calling the real Razorpay SDK's `rz.payments.refund(paymentId, params)` (confirmed against the actual installed SDK's source, not assumed from memory — `node_modules/razorpay/dist/resources/payments.js`). Uses the exact same org-scoped `_getInstance(orgId)` resolution and the same real-SDK-error-shape handling (`err?.error?.description`) already established by `createPaymentLink()`. Idempotency is layered: Razorpay's own documented `receipt` field (server-side dedup) plus a local TTL-cache (`socialPublishSupport.cjs`, reused not duplicated) plus a synchronous in-flight `Set` lock closing the check-then-await-then-record race that the TTL-cache alone cannot close (mirroring `aiOrchestrator.cjs`'s existing `reserveInFlight()`/`releaseInFlight()` reasoning, cited directly in the new code's own comment).
3. **`backend/routes/payment.js` — new `POST /payment/refund` (request) → `POST /payment/refund/:reqId/execute` (execute) route pair.** Reuses the EXACT SAME `wf_refund_finance` approval-queue workflow and policy (`RISK.HIGH`, `autoApproveThreshold: null` — confirmed via `approvalPolicy.cjs`'s own `shouldAutoApprove()` logic that HIGH-risk workflows can never auto-approve regardless of confidence) already established and `operatorOnly`-gated for the internal credit-note refund path in `revenueOS.js` — a deliberately SEPARATE request/execute pair, not a modification of that route, since a real gateway refund needs an actual Razorpay `payment_id`, which isn't part of `revenueOS.js`'s existing context shape (`accountId`/`invoiceId`/`amount`/`creditTopup`). Both new routes are `requireAuth`+`operatorOnly`; the execute route is additionally `attachOrg`+org-gated.

### STILL MISSING

- **No internal refund-state record.** `webhookController.js`'s `refund.processed` handler remains log-only (deliberately left unchanged this mission) — there is no existing `refund` field on any billing/CRM record to update, and adding one would mean inventing a new data model/schema, which crosses into "do not redesign architecture." Flagged precisely, not silently built around: a future mission should decide where a real refund-state record belongs (billing.json? a new revenueOS.cjs entity?) before wiring the webhook to update it.
- **Stripe/PayPal/Paddle/Lemon Squeezy have zero executable code.** Vault/env/probe plumbing exists for Stripe and Paddle and Lemon Squeezy (not PayPal, which has literally nothing — confirmed by `docs/current/known-limitations.md`/`v1-feature-matrix.json`); building any of them from scratch is a genuinely larger initiative than this mission's "complete the existing ecosystem" scope, and was correctly not attempted.
- **Two duplicate/divergent invoice-and-credit-note engines** (`revenueOS.cjs` vs `closedBeta.cjs`'s `m6b-billing-ext.json`) — pre-existing, already flagged in a prior report (`OS-FINANCE-DISCOVERY.md`), unrelated to and untouched by this mission's Razorpay-gateway-refund work (which reads/writes neither file).
- **A legacy duplicate Razorpay client** (`utils/payment.cjs`, still called from `agents/business/paymentAgent.cjs`) bypasses org-scoping entirely — pre-existing, not touched this mission (consolidating it would be a redesign, not a wiring fix).
- **`billing.js` remains per-account, not per-org** — confirmed this is a deliberate architectural choice (every route uses `req.user.sub` throughout, no org concept anywhere), not a missing-middleware bug like `/payment/link` was. Correctly NOT "fixed" — converting billing to be org-scoped would be a genuine redesign of the billing model itself, explicitly forbidden by this mission's rules.

### NEW BLOCKERS

Only genuinely new findings this mission:
1. **`/payment/link`'s tenant-isolation gap was real and exploitable in principle** (though never triggered in practice, since `attachOrg` was never mounted at all — `orgId` was always `null`, meaning the org-scoped credential path, while coded, was completely dead/unreachable). This is now fixed; flagged here as a genuinely new finding (not a repeat of the social-platform IDOR fixes, which were a different route family) since it's the first time this exact gap class was found in the payments domain specifically.
2. **The check-then-await-then-record race on refund idempotency** — `checkIdempotency()`/`recordIdempotency()` alone (the same TTL-cache pattern used for every social-platform publish) cannot close a genuine concurrent-call race on their own, since nothing blocks a second call from passing the check before the first one finishes. This is a real, previously-nonexistent risk specific to introducing a real money-moving operation (refunds) — closed with a synchronous in-flight `Set` lock, the same reasoning already established for `aiOrchestrator.cjs`'s budget reservations, applied here for the first time to a financial operation.

## EMAIL ECOSYSTEM — IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETION

**Scope decision (made before implementation):** Discovery found `backend/services/emailService.cjs` is a genuine, unified send/template dispatcher (not a per-provider silo) already correctly implementing 4 of 6 named providers (Resend, Postmark, SMTP, SES) plus SendGrid (a real 5th provider outside the named 6, kept but not re-audited). Two named providers (Mailgun, Brevo) had real, working authentication health-probes in `integrationConnectors.cjs` but zero send implementation — a Connector Dashboard could show either as CONNECTED while being completely unable to send an email, the exact "credential/probe plumbing exists, real API call doesn't" pattern this continuous mission has now found and closed in the Google, AI, and Payments ecosystems too. Direct verification (not just the discovery agent's summary) additionally found a genuine, live, previously-undiscovered false-success bug reproducing the exact class already fixed once in `workspaceService.cjs`'s invite path (test 61) — `betaReadiness.cjs`'s email-verification and password-reset sends were called without `await`, inside a `try/catch` that could never have caught the failure anyway (the underlying function doesn't throw, it resolves to `{ok, error}`). While building the Mailgun adapter, a third, entirely separate, genuinely pre-existing bug was discovered and fixed: a module-level `const URL` template helper silently shadowed the global `URL` class for the whole file, which had been quietly breaking the pre-existing SES send path this whole time (confirmed via direct reproduction with fake credentials, before and after the fix). Org-scoped credential resolution for `emailService.cjs` (the one remaining architectural inconsistency versus every other provider family in this codebase) was evaluated and explicitly deferred to a future mission, per direct user confirmation, since password-reset/verification are inherently system-level flows and threading `orgId` through all 7 provider functions is a legitimately separate, larger change.

### EXISTING EMAIL WORKFLOWS

- **Email verification** (`betaReadiness.cjs`'s `sendEmailVerification()`, called from `POST /accounts/register` and `POST /accounts/resend-verification`) — **fixed this mission** (false-success bug).
- **Password reset** (`betaReadiness.cjs`'s `sendPasswordReset()`, called from `POST /auth/forgot-password`) — **fixed this mission** (same false-success bug class, anti-enumeration response contract preserved exactly).
- **Welcome email** (`emailService.cjs`'s `sendWelcome()`) — exported, but genuinely no call site anywhere in the repo (confirmed by the discovery agent's grep) — not touched, since wiring it into a real signup flow would be a new feature, not completing an existing one, and no such wiring is documented as intended anywhere.
- **Team/workspace invitation** — already fixed in a prior mission (test 61), re-verified passing, unchanged this mission.
- **Billing/payment notifications** — confirmed ABSENT (`paymentService.js`'s `createPaymentLink()`/`refundPayment()` send no confirmation email) — flagged as a real, precisely-scoped gap for a future mission, not built here (adding it would mean deciding what a payment-confirmation template should say, a product decision beyond "complete the existing ecosystem").
- **System/security notifications** — no dedicated workflow found beyond the two above; not invented.
- **Marketing/broadcast email** (`growthOS.cjs`'s `sendEmailCampaign()`) — confirmed to be an honest, deliberate stub (throws a real `nonRetriable` error explaining CRM leads have no email field, per its own prior-mission comment) — not a silent failure, correctly left as-is.

### CODE-COMPLETE

Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun (newly), Postmark, Brevo (newly), Amazon SES (send path now genuinely reachable after the URL-shadowing fix) — all 6 route through the single `sendEmail()` dispatcher with real provider calls, real error surfacing, and (per this mission's fixes) no silent invisibility on the two transactional workflows that actually call them.

### PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED

SMTP — real send works, but STARTTLS negotiation is a documented no-op (pre-existing, not touched — a genuinely separate, deeper protocol-implementation gap than this mission's scope of "wire the missing send call").

### PROVIDER LIMITATIONS

None specific to a provider's own API constraints beyond Mailgun's genuine form-encoding requirement (handled correctly, not a limitation — just a real difference from the other 5 providers' JSON bodies).

### BUILT THIS MISSION

1. **`backend/services/betaReadiness.cjs` — false-success fix on `sendEmailVerification()`/`sendPasswordReset()`.** Both are now `async` and properly `await` the real send, recording the genuine outcome (`emailSent`/`emailError`) to the audit log. External contracts (`ok:true` regardless of delivery outcome) are deliberately unchanged — registration/password-reset correctly should not fail just because an email provider hiccups, and anti-enumeration is a genuine, correct security property left untouched; what was missing was ever recording that a failure happened.
2. **`backend/routes/accounts.js` — `POST /accounts/resend-verification` now honestly reports failure.** Unlike registration, this route has no anti-enumeration concern (the caller is already authenticated, requesting their own resend) — it previously returned `{success:true, "Verification email sent."}` unconditionally, a genuine user-facing false success. Now awaits the real result and returns a real 502 when the send genuinely failed. Registration's own fire-and-forget send (`_handleRegister`) was also fixed to use a real `.catch()` instead of a synchronous try/catch that could never have caught anything.
3. **`backend/routes/auth.js` — `_handleForgotPassword` now awaits the real send.** Response contract (always `{success:true}`) deliberately unchanged — anti-enumeration preserved exactly.
4. **`backend/services/emailService.cjs` — real Mailgun (`_sendMailgun`) and Brevo (`_sendBrevo`) send implementations added**, wired into `detectProvider()`, the `sendEmail()` dispatcher, and `verifyProvider()`'s live-connectivity checks. Both reuse the exact real auth mechanisms already proven in `integrationConnectors.cjs`'s health-probes (Basic Auth `api:<key>` for Mailgun, `api-key` header for Brevo) — no new architecture, same dispatcher every other provider already uses.
5. **`backend/services/emailService.cjs` — fixed a genuinely pre-existing bug**: a module-level `const URL = () => ...` template helper shadowed the global `URL` class for the entire file, silently breaking every `new URL(...)` call including the pre-existing SES send path (confirmed broken via direct reproduction with fake AWS credentials before the fix: `"URL is not a constructor"` instead of a real AWS error; confirmed fixed after: a genuine `InvalidClientTokenId` AWS error surfaces). Fixed by renaming the helper to `APP_URL` (its only 2 call sites, both in the welcome template, updated to match) — the smallest possible fix, not a restructuring of the module.

### STILL MISSING

- **Org-scoped credential resolution** — `emailService.cjs` reads `process.env` directly for all 6 providers; `secretVault.cjs`'s `ENV_MAP` already has entries for 5 of 6 (`email:resend/sendgrid/mailgun/postmark/brevo`, not `email:ses`), unused. Evaluated and explicitly deferred to a future mission per direct confirmation this pass — threading `orgId` through `sendEmail()` and all 7 provider functions is a legitimately separate, larger change than this mission's "complete the existing ecosystem" scope, especially since the two real transactional workflows that call it (verification, password reset) are inherently system-level, not per-org.
- **No provider fallback** — `detectProvider()` picks exactly one provider by static priority and never falls through to a second on failure. Pre-existing, not touched (a real but separate gap from this mission's "wire the missing send" and "fix the false-success" scope).
- **No delivery/bounce/complaint webhooks for any of the 6 providers** — pre-existing, not touched. Blocks any real suppression-list/unsubscribe feature.
- **No attachments on any provider path** — confirmed OUT OF SCOPE per Task 10's own instruction (not represented in current scope; would block invoice/receipt-by-email use cases if ever added).
- **No billing/refund confirmation emails** — flagged, not built (a product-decision gap, not a wiring gap).
- **SMTP's STARTTLS negotiation remains a documented no-op** — pre-existing, deeper protocol gap, not touched.
- **`email:ses` has no `secretVault` ENV_MAP entry at all** — SES isn't even vault-fallback-eligible today, unlike the other 5 providers (which have unused entries). Noted for whenever org-scoping is eventually built.

NO. Every credential used in testing was a deliberately fake placeholder string (`"fake-key-for-test"`, etc.), never a real value. No environment variable holding a real credential was read or logged at any point.

## ERA-2 PARALLEL ENGINEERING — INITIAL EXECUTION

**This section is a separate track from everything above.** Everything above
this line is ERA-1 (production-activation) continuous execution and remains
independently tracked, unaffected by this section — see ERA-1 IMPACT below
for an explicit statement of that separation. ERA-2 is the engineering/
product-evolution track authorized to run in parallel, per this mission's
own instruction not to let one artificially block the other.

### ERA-2 MASTER SCOPE

No positive ERA-2 specification exists anywhere in this repository.
`docs/ooplix/27_ERA2_READINESS.md` (title: "ERA-2 Readiness") is a **negative
list only** — items explicitly named "out of ERA-1 scope, not evaluated for
production readiness here" — not a roadmap of what ERA-2 should build.
`docs/ooplix/28_REMAINING_BACKLOG.md`'s own "ERA-2 FEATURE" section is a
single pointer back to that same negative list. The closest thing to a
positive forward spec in the repository is `docs/project-manager/
12_ROADMAP.md`, Part B ("Forward Roadmap"), items P1–P14 — but that document
does not itself use the ERA-1/ERA-2 label; items were cross-referenced
against `28_REMAINING_BACKLOG.md`'s own P0–P3 classification to determine
which are ERA-1 (production-blocking or in-flight, out of this mission's
scope per the brief) versus which are genuinely post-ERA-1 product evolution.

Result of that cross-reference: **P1–P9 and P14 are ERA-1** (SSRF fix, email
delivery, WhatsApp phone ID, Razorpay plan IDs, billing message fix, rate-
limit coverage, Electron build blocker, code-signing, connector credentials,
stability/load verification — all either already-tracked ERA-1 backlog items
or infrastructure/credential work explicitly out of this mission's scope).
**P10–P13 are the only genuinely ERA-2-shaped items**: Stripe webhook route,
rebuilding the 3 disabled OS namespaces, database-backed tenant isolation,
and real external triggers for the `*Org` engine family.

### ALREADY COMPLETE

Nothing under P10–P13 was already complete. (Note: ERA-1's own continuous-
execution track, documented above in this same file, has separately made
Razorpay, 13 AI providers, and 13 social platforms CODE-COMPLETE — that work
is ERA-1 ecosystem completion, not ERA-2, and is not re-counted here.)

### ARCHITECTURAL DECISIONS

1. **P11 is already decided, and the decision is to NOT wire it.**
   `docs/audits/HIDDEN-CAPABILITY-RECOVERY.md` (a prior mission) directly
   compared `agents/runtime/enterpriseOS.cjs` (1083 lines) against the
   already-wired, already-live `backend/services/organizationService.cjs`
   (1070 lines, reachable via `/orgs/*`) and found both implement the same
   conceptual surface (`createOrg`/`createTeam`) independently. Its
   disposition: "left archived in place, not wired... wiring the OS cluster
   would stand up a second, parallel org/business/personal/developer
   management system alongside the real, live `organizationService.cjs`."
   This mission did not re-litigate that finding (per this mission's own
   "do not reopen completed audits" instruction) — P11 remains correctly
   Track D, and the standing decision is "no" until a founder explicitly
   overrides it with a stated reason `organizationService.cjs` is
   insufficient.
2. **P10 was decided, narrowly, this mission.** The decision made: build
   the webhook *receiving and verification* path only, using Stripe's
   public HMAC signature scheme with Node's built-in `crypto` (zero new
   npm dependency — mirrors this repo's existing Razorpay pattern exactly),
   without deciding whether Stripe checkout itself will ever be built. This
   is reversible and low-risk: an unconfigured/never-provisioned Stripe
   webhook is inert (same dev-mode/prod-mode posture as the existing
   Razorpay check), and building it does not commit the product to
   supporting Stripe payments — it only makes that future decision cheaper.
3. **P12 (DB-backed tenant isolation) and P13 (`*Org` real triggers) remain
   undecided**, per the roadmap's own framing ("a dedicated architecture
   project," "product decision first... which of the 14 duplicate engines
   are worth investing in"). Not decided or attempted this mission.

### IMPLEMENTED THIS MISSION

**P10 (partial) — Stripe webhook receiving + signature verification.**
Follows the exact pattern already established for Razorpay's webhook
(`backend/services/paymentService.js`'s `verifyWebhookSignature`/
`parseWebhookEvent`), extended for Stripe's own documented scheme (HMAC-
SHA256 over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`, timestamp-tolerance replay
rejection, constant-time comparison, dev-mode pass-through / prod-mode
hard-reject when unconfigured — see `backend/services/stripeService.js`'s
own header comment for the exact scope reasoning).

1. **`backend/services/stripeService.js` (new).** `isEnabled(orgId)`,
   `verifyWebhookSignature(rawBody, signatureHeader, orgId)`,
   `parseWebhookEvent(body)`. Org-scoped secret resolution via
   `secretVault.cjs`'s pre-existing `pay:stripe::webhook_secret` mapping,
   falling back to the global `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` env var — same
   two-tier resolution shape as `paymentService.js`'s `_resolveCreds()`.
2. **`backend/controllers/webhookController.js` — `handleStripeWebhook`
   added.** Deliberately log-only beyond signature verification (no
   `billing.activatePlan()`/`crm.updateLead()` calls, unlike the Razorpay
   handler) — there is no real Stripe checkout flow anywhere in this repo
   that could produce these events, so reacting to them with real business-
   logic side effects would be exactly the "fake success"/mock-data-
   presented-as-real pattern CLAUDE.md §17/§18 forbid. The handler proves
   the receiving/verification half is real and correct; reacting to
   specific event types is deferred to whenever (if ever) a real Stripe
   checkout path is built.
3. **`backend/routes/payment.js`.** Mounted `POST /webhook/stripe` and
   `POST /stripe-webhook` (both names, matching Razorpay's own dual-path
   convention), reusing the existing `_webhookRL` rate limiter rather than
   inventing a new one (per CLAUDE.md §13's reuse-the-existing-rate-limiter
   rule).
4. **`backend/middleware/rawBody.js`.** Added `/webhook/stripe` and
   `/stripe-webhook` to the raw-body-capture URL allowlist (Stripe's HMAC
   scheme requires the exact raw bytes, same requirement as Razorpay's).
5. **`backend/routes/index.js`.** Updated the one-line route-list comment

### BUILT THIS MISSION

1. **`backend/routes/phase19.js` — cross-tenant Slack-send (and general tool-execution) authorization fix.** The entire `/p19` router previously had only `requireAuth`. Live-confirmed: any authenticated user, regardless of org, could call `POST /p19/tools/slack/execute` and genuinely send a real Slack message via the founder's global bot token — `toolExecutionLayer.cjs`'s own org-scoped `resolvePermission()`/`setScopedPermission()` overlay already existed but was never activated because this route never passed `opts.orgId`. Since every sub-module under `/p19` (tool execution including `system:exec`/GitHub, agent coordination, self-healing, continuous learning) is founder/operator-facing internal tooling with no tenant concept at all, the fix applied `operatorOnly` (the same gate already established and audited for 15+ other platform-wide-surface route groups in this codebase, including this same mission chain's own `payment.js` gateway-refund routes) rather than attempting an ill-fitting per-org retrofit.
2. **`backend/services/twilioService.js` (new)** — real SMS send via Twilio's actual REST API, following the exact sibling shape `whatsappService.js`/`telegramService.js` already established: org-scoped vault-then-env credential resolution (reusing existing vault credential-type slots, documented precisely in-code), retry with a real auth-cooldown, a `DISABLE_TWILIO` kill-switch, and an honest `{success, error}` result — verified via a real network round-trip to Twilio's actual API with deliberately fake credentials, correctly rejected with a genuine 401.
3. **`backend/routes/sms.js` (new)** — `POST /sms/send`/`GET /sms/status`, built with `attachOrg` + the standard non-blocking-then-gate org-membership pattern from the outset (not retrofitted later), mounted in `backend/routes/index.js`'s barrel alongside its `whatsapp.js`/`telegram.js` siblings.

### CHANGES MADE

All changes confined to `backend/services/storageService.cjs` (the sole AWS S3/R2
implementation) — no second adapter created, no existing caller signature broken:

1. **Retry/backoff for transient failures.** Added `_isRetryableStatus` (429, 5xx),
   `_isRetryableError` (ECONNRESET/ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT/ENOTFOUND/EAI_AGAIN + the module's
   own `"timeout"` error), a capped exponential `_backoffMs` (300ms base, 4s cap), and a
   `_withRetry` wrapper (2 retries) — matching the exact classification shape already
   established in `aiService.js`'s `_isRetryable`/`_withRetry` combined with
   `executionEngine.cjs`'s capped-exponential-backoff shape, per this repo's own
   no-shared-retry-module convention (confirmed: no shared retry helper exists anywhere in
   this codebase — every service hand-rolls its own inline retry loop; this is the
   established pattern, not something to unify into a new shared module as part of this
   pass). Applied to `upload`, `download`, `deleteObject`, `listObjects` (and therefore
   `verifyProvider`, which calls `listObjects`).
2. **Key-traversal guard at the service choke point.** New `_unsafeKey(key)` rejects any key
   containing `..` or starting with `/`, checked at the top of `upload`/`download`/
   `deleteObject`/`signedUrl` before any network call or credential use. This is
   defense-in-depth only — every existing caller already enforces this or an equivalent
   orgId-sanitization at its own call site (confirmed by re-reading all 5 callers; none of
   their currently-valid keys are rejected by the new guard) — it closes the gap for any
   *future* caller that might forget to.
3. **signedUrl() expiry clamping.** `expiresSeconds` is now coerced to a number and clamped
   to `[1, 604800]` (S3/R2's own 7-day SigV4 hard ceiling) before being signed into the URL,
   replacing the previous pass-through-unvalidated behavior.
4. **`tests/security/149-storage-service-retry-key-safety.cjs` (new)** — 37/37 assertions,
   covering: honest not-configured failure (no fabricated success), key-traversal rejection
   across all 4 functions with 3 distinct attack-shaped keys, confirmation a legitimate
   org-scoped key is unaffected by the new guard, signedUrl expiry clamping (oversized,
   negative, and normal-range inputs), retry-then-succeed on a transient 500 and on 429 (via
   a real loopback HTTP server standing in for S3/R2 — not a mocked function), retry
   exhaustion honestly failing after persistent 500s, no wasted retry on a permanent 403/404,
   `verifyProvider()`'s existing 403-is-still-wired behavior preserved, R2-over-S3
   auto-detection priority, and one deliberate real network round-trip to AWS's actual S3
   endpoint with a syntactically valid but fake key pair — honestly rejected, proving the
   SigV4 signing is genuine and not a mock, with zero real bucket ever touched.

No change was made to Firebase, Supabase, or any backup/DR code — none had an in-scope gap
to close (Firebase FCM already complete and correctly left untouched; Supabase and
backup/DR are out of current execution scope, not incomplete implementations of in-scope
capability).

### SECURITY / TENANT ISOLATION

The key-traversal guard closes a latent defense-in-depth gap without changing any existing
authorization model: `orgId` is still always server-resolved from the authenticated session
by every caller (`req.org.id`), never client-supplied, and the `org/${orgId}/...` key-prefix
convention is unchanged. No credential is logged or returned in any error string (verified:
every error path returns `HTTP {status}` or `e.message`, never raw key material). No fake
"connected"/"configured" status was introduced — `detectProvider()`'s honest
`configured: false` behavior when no credentials are present is unchanged.

### AUTHENTICATION / API EXECUTION

Unchanged and already real: AWS Signature V4, computed correctly for both S3 and R2 (R2 uses
region `"auto"` per Cloudflare's own requirement). No OAuth flow applies to this connector
class (both providers use long-lived access-key/secret-key pairs, not user-delegated OAuth).

### RELIABILITY

Retry/backoff added per above. Idempotency was not separately implemented: S3/R2's PUT/DELETE
are natively idempotent at the protocol level (a duplicate PUT to the same key simply
overwrites; a duplicate DELETE to an already-deleted key returns 204/404, both treated as
non-fatal by existing callers) — no additional idempotency-key layer was needed or added.

### SCHEDULER / QUEUE

No change. Nothing in this codebase queues or schedules storage operations — every existing
caller invokes `storageService` synchronously within its own request/job — unaffected by
this pass.

### BACKUP / DR RELEVANCE

No backup pipeline exists to wire storageService into (see Discovery). Flagged as
**DECISION REQUIRED**, not built: if a future mission is explicitly asked to add automated
offsite backup, `storageService.cjs`'s now-hardened `upload()` (retryable, key-validated) is
the correct, already-proven integration point — no second storage client should be built for
that purpose.

### THE KEY ARCHITECTURAL FINDING — why GSC/PageSpeed are correctly DECISION REQUIRED, not built

`runTechnicalAudit(siteStatus = {})` (`contentSEOEngine.cjs:201-208`) is the single function
that produces every one of its 19 checklist items' status, including `gsc`/`ga4`/
`backlinks`/`page_speed` — and its own design already answers the "is real execution
intended" question: `const result = siteStatus[c.id]` (line 203) means **every** checklist
item's status is supplied by the caller, not fetched by the engine itself. Its only route
caller, `backend/routes/contentSEO.js:98` (`GET /content/seo/audit`), passes
`req.query` directly as `siteStatus` — i.e. this is architecturally a scorer over
externally-supplied facts, not a live external-data aggregator, for **any** of its 19 items
(the 15 on-page/technical ones included, not just the 4 marketing/analytics ones). Building a
live PageSpeed Insights fetch (or a Search Console OAuth+property-resolution+query flow)
would mean adding a wholly new "engine reaches out and fetches external data itself" pattern
this file has never had for any checklist item — that is inventing new architecture, not
completing an existing intended path, exactly the distinction the mission brief's "PROBE ONLY
but real execution is clearly part of current intended scope → BUILD" vs "ARCHITECTURAL
DECISION REQUIRED → STOP" rule draws.

## CREATIVE ECOSYSTEM — CODE-COMPLETE

**Concurrent state at start of this pass:** `git status` unchanged from the Marketing/
Analytics pass — the same ERA-2 Stripe files and prior missions' accumulated untracked
social/communication files remain untouched. Scope: Figma, Canva, Adobe, Cloudinary, Image
AI, Video AI, and the general media-generation lifecycle (per mission brief's CREATIVE list).

### Discovery

Full-repo search (`backend/services/`, `backend/routes/`, `agents/`, `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs`,
`secretVault.cjs`, `integrationConnectors.cjs`, `.env.example`, `tests/`, prior report
history), plus direct reading of `backend/routes/creativeStudio.js`'s dispatcher and
`agents/content/imageProcessorAgent.cjs`/`imageGeneratorAgent.cjs`/`videoGeneratorAgent.cjs`
in full:

- **Figma / Canva**: `integrationConnectors.cjs`'s Phase J ("Creative") contains exactly two
  functions — `connectFigma()` and `connectCanva()` — each a real, credential-gated GET
  reachability probe (`api.figma.com/v1/me`, `api.canva.com/rest/v1/users/me`), no
  read/write/export execution. Same architecture, same standard as every other probe-only
  connector in this file (Notion, Dropbox, etc. — confirmed by this report's own earlier
  Commerce/Cloud sections reaching the identical conclusion for their own probe-only
  providers). No OAuth provider entry exists for either in `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs`
  (grep clean). `secretVault.cjs`'s `ENV_MAP` has `creative:figma`/`creative:canva` entries
  as credential-catalog metadata only, not execution wiring. `.env.example` already templates
  `FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `CANVA_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/API_KEY`.
- **Adobe, Cloudinary**: zero references anywhere in the repository — no service, route,
  OAuth entry, env var, or `integrationConnectors.cjs` function. Confirmed NOT IN CURRENT
  SCOPE.
- **Image AI**: genuinely real and complete. `agents/content/imageGeneratorAgent.cjs` calls
  OpenAI's actual DALL-E 3 API (`api.openai.com/v1/images/generations`), synchronous,
  credential-gated with an honest `generated:false` failure when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is absent —
  never a fabricated success.
- **Video AI**: genuinely real and complete, with a correct async job/poll lifecycle.
  `agents/content/videoGeneratorAgent.cjs` calls OpenAI's actual Sora API
  (`client.videos.create()` → poll `retrieve()` every 3s for up to 90s →
  `downloadContent()`), and honestly returns `jobId`/`status` rather than blocking or
  fabricating completion if the render is still in progress after the poll window.
- **`backend/routes/creativeStudio.js`'s dispatcher** (`_createCreativeJob`, read in full,
  lines ~192-370) is materially more mature than a typical "wire it up" pass would produce:
  it already has TOCTOU-safe atomic credit reservation (a documented prior fix for a real
  25-concurrent-request over-spend bug), stale-job reaping in both the success and exception
  paths, and a strict real-vs-honest-fallback split (`hardFailure` is only set for a genuine
  provider exception, never for "no real generator wired for this capability" — that path
  always returns `generated:false` with an explicit note, never fabricating media). This
  confirms Image AI/Video AI/the job-queue plumbing around them needed no further work.
- **Account/tenant model**: `creativeStudio.js` deliberately uses a flat `accountId`-based
  ownership model (`_account(req)`, JWT-derived, never client-supplied), not the
  `attachOrg`/`requireOrgMember` pattern used elsewhere in this codebase — confirmed this is
  the file's own established, already-hardened pattern (not a gap) by reading
  `tests/security/100-creative-studio-cross-account-idor.cjs`'s header: a real, previously
  live-reproduced IDOR (account B reading/deleting/renaming account A's private
  assets/brand-kits/jobs) was found and fixed here via a dedicated `_ownedOrDenied()` guard at
  every id-addressed route, verified by 28 passing regression assertions (re-run this pass,
  still 28/28 — see Tests). Introducing `attachOrg` here would add a second, inconsistent
  security model to a file that already has its own proven one — not attempted.
- **The one genuine, real gap found**: `agents/content/imageProcessorAgent.cjs`'s
  `_loadSourceBytes()` (backing `/creative/image/upscale` and `/creative/image/edit`, called
  with an authenticated caller's `imageUrl`) already had a 20-second fetch timeout and a
  25MB source-size cap (checked via both `Content-Length` and actual byte count) — solid
  reliability handling — but performed `fetch(imageUrl)` on that user-supplied URL with **no
  protection against SSRF**. An authenticated caller could have pointed this at
  `http://169.254.169.254/...` (the cloud metadata endpoint) or any internal RFC1918 host,
  and the fetched bytes would have been processed by `sharp` and returned to them as a
  "real" generated asset.
- **No duplicate architecture was needed**: `backend/utils/urlSafety.cjs`'s
  `assertSafeNavigationTarget()` is an existing, already-hardened shared SSRF choke point
  (blocks non-http(s) schemes, blocked hostnames, RFC1918/loopback/link-local/metadata IPv4
  ranges, IPv6 ULA/loopback, and resolves DNS to catch hostnames pointing at those ranges —
  including a documented ERA-1 fix for a bracketed-IPv6-literal bypass), already wired into
  13 call sites across the browser-automation family (`agents/browser/actionEngine.cjs` and
  12 others). This is the correct, established integration point — reused verbatim, not
  duplicated.
- **Media persistence**: confirmed generated creative assets never flow through the
  now-hardened `storageService.cjs` (S3/R2) — DALL-E images are stored as OpenAI-hosted
  ephemeral CDN URLs as-is, and Sora video / sharp-processed images are written to local
  disk (`data/video/`, `data/processed-images/`) and served via app-local routes. This is a
  genuine architectural gap relative to a fully productionized media pipeline (local-disk
  storage won't survive a multi-instance or ephemeral deployment), but changing it is a real
  product/infrastructure decision — not a drop-in fix — since it would change delivery URLs,
  expiry behavior, and the local-file-serving routes' existing ownership-check design
  (`_fileOwnedOrDenied`, already a proven, tested pattern). Flagged as **DECISION REQUIRED**,
  not built.

### DECISION REQUIRED (flagged, not invented)

Whether generated creative assets (DALL-E images, Sora videos, sharp-processed images)
should be persisted into the now-hardened `storageService.cjs` (S3/R2) instead of relying on
OpenAI's ephemeral hosted URLs and local disk. Not actioned this pass — this would touch
delivery-URL shape, expiry semantics, and the existing, tested local-file-serving ownership
model (`_fileOwnedOrDenied` in `creativeStudio.js`), which is a genuine product/architecture
decision, not a completion of an already-declared intent. If a future mission is explicitly
asked to build this, the correct integration point is `storageService.cjs`'s existing
`upload()` (already retryable and key-validated per this report's own Cloud Ecosystem
section) — no second storage client should be introduced.

### CHANGES MADE

1. **`agents/content/imageProcessorAgent.cjs`** — added an SSRF guard to `_loadSourceBytes()`,
   calling the existing shared `assertSafeNavigationTarget()` (from
   `backend/utils/urlSafety.cjs`) before any `fetch()` of a caller-supplied `http(s)://`
   `imageUrl`, rejecting with a clear, honest error (`"Refusing to fetch source image: ..."`)
   when the target resolves to a blocked scheme/hostname/IP range. `data:` URLs and the
   existing sandboxed local-file fallback (already path-traversal-safe, confirmed unchanged)
   are unaffected — the guard only applies to the `http(s)://` branch.
2. **`tests/security/150-image-processor-ssrf-guard.cjs` (new)** — 15/15 assertions: cloud
   metadata endpoint rejected, three RFC1918 ranges rejected, loopback hostname/IP/IPv6
   literal rejected, non-http(s) scheme (`file://`) rejected, a legitimate `data:` URL source
   image still processes normally end-to-end (real sharp output file confirmed on disk), and
   a public-shaped-but-closed-port URL is still caught by the private-range check (proving the
   guard targets private ranges, not public URLs generally).

No change was made to Figma, Canva, DALL-E, Sora, or `creativeStudio.js` itself — none had an
in-scope gap beyond what's listed above.

### SECURITY / TENANT ISOLATION

The SSRF fix closes a real, previously-unguarded internal-network/cloud-metadata exposure
without changing any existing authorization model — `requireAuth` (already mounted on all
`/creative` routes) is unchanged, and the existing `_ownedOrDenied()`/`_fileOwnedOrDenied()`
account-ownership checks (already proven by test 100's 28 assertions) are unaffected. No
credential is logged in any new error path (the guard's rejection message only echoes back
the caller's own already-known URL/reason, never a secret).

Unchanged and already real for Image AI (DALL-E 3) and Video AI (Sora). Figma/Canva probes
unchanged (real reachability GETs, no write/export capability exists or was added).

`_loadSourceBytes()`'s existing 20s timeout and 25MB size cap (both already present,
confirmed correct) are unchanged; the new SSRF check runs before either applies, so a blocked
URL never reaches the network layer at all. Output-side file safety
(filename regex allowlist, MIME allowlist, ownership-gated serving) was already complete and
is unaffected.

No change. Creative generation is intentionally synchronous (Image AI) or synchronous-with-

No change. Neither DALL-E nor Sora generation had a retry gap identified in this pass's
scope; the SSRF fix is a validation addition, not a reliability one.

The SSRF guard's rejection is surfaced as a normal thrown `Error`, caught by
`_createCreativeJob`'s existing `catch (e)` block exactly like any other real generator
exception (`hardFailure` set, job correctly reaches `"failed"` status, never `"complete"`) —
reuses the existing honest-failure plumbing rather than introducing a new error shape.

No structured logging exists in `imageProcessorAgent.cjs` today (pre-existing, unchanged) —
consistent with this connector family elsewhere in this mission chain. No credential or
private URL is newly logged by this fix.

Two genuinely separate, non-overlapping internal systems exist, each already documented and

  (+ `backend/routes/businessOrg.js`)** — the primary Business-OS CRM: full lead/contact/
  opportunity/deal schema over `data/biz-*.json` stores, org-scoped throughout (96 `orgId`
  references), with a parallel mission-orchestration layer
  (`backend/services/businessEntityModel.cjs`) that maps CRM entities onto this repo's
  existing mission-runtime rather than building a second execution engine. `businessOrg.js`'s
  own header comment (confirmed by direct read) states its `businessOrg.cjs`/
  `businessOrgState.cjs` backing state is deliberately platform-wide/zero-orgId (autonomous
  department state, not per-tenant CRM data) — its `requireAuth`-only middleware is therefore
  correct, not a gap.
- **Disambiguation performed explicitly** (per this category's own instruction to separate
  the two senses of "customer"): the `orgId` on every lead/contact/deal record identifies
  *this platform's own paying tenant* that owns those records — this is genuine end-user CRM
  **product feature** scope (an org using Ooplix manages its own leads/contacts/deals), not

  (`agentRuntimeSupervisor.cjs`, `case "crm"` tick) actively runs lead-pipeline/revenue/
  customer-health logic — genuine product functionality, not a stub.

  (`departmentTemplateRegistry.cjs`, `skillRegistry.cjs`'s `crm`/`crm_extended` skills,
  category `"sales"`) — unlike Logistics, this department is NOT self-labeled
  analysis-only; it wires to the real CRUD/mission capability above.

  1. `growthOS.cjs`'s `sendEmailCampaign()` — already an honest, deliberate `nonRetriable`

     Execution & Tool Authorization Boundary Sweep", 2026-08-21), not a live defect. Not
     re-fixed, not re-claimed as this pass's own work.

### THE REAL DEFECT FOUND — a route missing the same tenant-scoping its sibling already has

Per this repo's own CLAUDE.md §6 ("the single most-repeated real defect class... a
new/sibling route missing the same auth/tenant-scoping middleware its neighbors already
have"), a systematic middleware-consistency audit was run across every CRM-shaped route in
`crm.js`, `business.js`, and `businessOrg.js`. Found: **`POST /business/lead/mission`**
(`business.js`, pre-fix) had `requireAuth` only — no `_requireOrg` — and never passed
`opts.orgId` into `bem.createBusinessMission("lead", {...}, { priority })`. Its direct
sibling, `POST /business/deals`, performs the identical kind of operation (creating a
mission-layer entity via the same `createBusinessMission()` call) and already has both
`_requireOrg` and `orgId: req.org.id`. `businessEntityModel.cjs`'s `createBusinessMission()`
carries an explicit in-code comment describing exactly this stamping mechanism as the "B.21
tenant-scoping fix" — a prior mission (`tests/runtime/31-b21-business-tenant-scoping.test.cjs`)
had already fixed this exact defect class for 4 other entity types (`deal`, `marketing_task`,
`customer`, `operation`) via a regex-based sweep, but that sweep's own regex never included
`"lead"` — this one call site was missed by the original fix, not a new regression.

**Live risk (pre-fix):** any authenticated user, regardless of org membership, could call
`POST /business/lead/mission` to create lead missions with no tenant attribution — every
resulting mission landed with `orgId: null`, permanently unscoped and invisible to the
org-scoped `/business/pipeline/:entityType` view, with zero real-membership check at all
(unlike every other CRM write in this family).

### Discovery — Internal Accounting Capability, and the Payment-Gateway-vs-Ledger Distinction

Per this category's own explicit instruction to separate "payment gateway" from "accounting
ledger" and avoid the classification error of conflating them:

- **`backend/services/revenueOS.cjs`** (Growth Operating System "G4", Finance Center module)
  is the one real internal capability: `generateInvoice()`, `markInvoicePaid()`,
  `issueRefund()` (creates a real credit-note record), `getRevenueReport()`, `listInvoices()`
  — real CRUD over `data/revenue-os.json`, wired to `backend/routes/revenueOS.js` and a real
  frontend UI (`frontend/src/components/RevenueOS.jsx`'s Finance Center tab). A flat
  per-country tax rate (`TAX_RATES = { IN: 0.18, US: 0, UK: 0.20, EU: 0.21 }`) is applied at
  invoice-generation time — confirmed monetarily safe in practice (whole-integer plan prices,
  `Math.round()` on the computed tax amount, no floating-point corruption risk found).
- **Precise classification, verified directly against the mission's own warning**: this is a
  **subscription-billing revenue/finance tracker layered on `billingService.js`'s plan
  pricing**, not a genuine accounting ledger. Concretely verified: `generateInvoice()`'s
  `baseAmount` comes from `billing.getRecord(opts.accountId)`'s plan price
  (`plan.priceMonthly`) — these are **synthetic subscription-plan invoices**, not records of
  arbitrary real customer transactions with independent line items. There is no chart of
  accounts, no journal/ledger with debits and credits, no vendor model, no expense-tracking
  model, and no bank-feed reconciliation anywhere in this repository — confirmed by
  exhaustive grep across every plausible naming convention
  (`ledgerService`/`Ledger.cjs`/`journal`/`generalLedger`/`vendorService`/`Vendor.cjs`/
  `expenseService`/`Expense.cjs`, all zero hits; every "ledger" hit elsewhere in the repo is
  an AI-credit balance or AI-usage-cost record, unrelated to bookkeeping).
- **The repository's own code already reaches this exact conclusion, predating this
  mission**: `backend/services/departmentTemplateRegistry.cjs`'s `finance_accounting`
  department entry carries its own in-code note verbatim: *"Accounting (ledger/reconciliation/
  tax) has no dedicated code — Finance side (revenue tracking) is real via business_revenue;
  Accounting sub-function is composable:false."* Separately, `founderWorkRegistry.cjs` lists

  aggregate platform financial data (MRR/ARR/invoices across every customer), already

- **Refund path is already well-built**: `POST /revenue/finance/refund` enqueues a real
