  `approved`/`auto_approved` and `!reqRecord.resumedAt` before calling `issueRefund()` —
  genuinely idempotent (a second execute call on the same approval request is rejected with
  `already_executed`), with an explicit "no rollback needed if rejected" design. No gap found;
  not touched.

### THE REAL DEFECT FOUND — a live false-success bug on a real financial write

Traced every real caller of `revenueOS.cjs`'s exported functions (not just the manual
operator routes) and found a genuine, live, previously-undiscovered bug:
**`backend/services/revenueAutomationEngine.cjs`'s `"prepare_invoice"` automation action**
called `generateInvoice(accountId, { amount, plan, period })` — **two positional
arguments** — but `generateInvoice(opts)` (in `revenueOS.cjs`) declares only **one**
parameter, a single options object. JavaScript silently drops an excess argument rather than
erroring, so `opts` inside `generateInvoice` was bound to the bare `accountId` **string**,
making `opts.accountId` always `undefined`.

**Live, reachable path confirmed** (not dead code): `POST /revenue-engine/automate/:action`
(`backend/routes/autonomousRevenue.js`, mounted at `requireAuth`+`operatorOnly` in
`backend/routes/index.js`) → `revenueAutomationEngine.automate("prepare_invoice", params)` →
`AUTOMATION_ACTIONS.prepare_invoice.requiresApproval` is `false`, so it executes
immediately, with no approval gate, unlike the manual refund path above.

**Concrete effect, pre-fix:** every automated invoice generated this way was silently
attributed to `accountId: undefined` (via `billing.getRecord(undefined)` creating/reading a
bogus trial billing record), silently ignored the caller's real `amount`/`plan`/`period`
(all fell back to that bogus trial record's plan price, effectively `₹0`), and the action
still reported `{ ok: true }` — **a real false-success on a real financial write**, precisely
what this mission's False Success Rule forbids.

A second, related instance of the same argument-shape defect class was found in the same
function: `"win_back_campaign"` called `createWinBackCampaign(accountId, { template,
discount })`, but `createWinBackCampaign(accountId, templateId)` expects `templateId` as a
plain **string** matched against `WINBACK_TEMPLATES`' real ids (`"wbt_1"`/`"wbt_2"`/
`"wbt_3"`). An object never strictly-equals a string id, so the wrong (always-first)
win-back template was silently used regardless of what was requested — additionally, the
caller's own default (`"standard"`) was not even a real template id, so this was broken by
default, not only on a mismatched object. Lower severity than the invoice bug (no
financial-amount fabrication, no false attribution) but the same underlying defect class and
fixed in the same pass since it lives in the identical function.

### THE REAL DEFECT FOUND — a second write path missing a fix its sibling already has

Reading `co3UserSuccess.cjs`'s already-documented "Phase B.15" fix closely revealed its own
comment (at `updateTicket()`) states: *"resolvedAt was set on 'resolved' but never cleared on
reopen, and 'closed' never set it at all (**inconsistent with replyToTicket, which handles
both**)"* — i.e., the original B.15 fix's author believed `replyToTicket()` already handled
enum validation and resolvedAt-on-reopen correctly, and therefore only fixed `updateTicket()`.
Direct inspection of `replyToTicket()` (pre-fix) showed that belief was incorrect: it wrote
`ticket.status = opts.status || ticket.status` with **zero enum validation**, and only ever
*set* `resolvedAt` on a terminal status — it never cleared it on reopen.

**Live, reachable path confirmed**: `POST /co3/cs/:id/reply` (`backend/routes/co3UserSuccess.js`)
passes `req.body` straight through as `opts` to `replyToTicket(id, opts)`, gated only by
`_assertTicketOwner` (a real ownership check, unaffected) — no status validation exists on
this path at all. A caller could `POST /co3/cs/:id/reply` with
`{"body": "...", "status": "DROP_TABLE"}` and reproduce the exact same corruption the
original B.15 fix closed for `updateTicket()`: the ticket silently vanishes from
`getCSInbox()`'s `byStatus`/`slaBreach` buckets (confirmed by direct reading of
`getCSInbox()`'s bucketing logic, which trusts `t.status` verbatim with no re-validation),
understating a support manager's real backlog. Separately, reopening a resolved ticket via a
reply (a normal, expected support workflow — "customer says it's not actually fixed") left
the stale `resolvedAt` timestamp in place, understating `avgResolutionHrs` the same way the
original bug did via the other write path.

### TENANT SECURITY

No change to any authorization model. Notion execution inherits `execute()`'s existing,
unmodified permission/rate-limit/retry/usage-logging pipeline exactly like every other tool
in this file — `delete_page`'s `risk: "high"` classification (pre-existing, unchanged) means
it is denied by default and receives zero automatic retries, matching `delete_file`/
`merge_pr`'s existing high-risk treatment. No client-controlled account/credential selection
was introduced — `_notionToken()` resolves the same way `connectNotion()` already did,
reading from server-side environment/vault state and the existing OAuth connection store,
never from client input.

### FILE / DOCUMENT SAFETY

Notion page operations validate required fields (`pageId`, `parentId`, `properties`) before
any network call, matching this file's existing convention for Gmail/Drive. No arbitrary
object is passed through unvalidated to the Notion API — `properties`/parent shape are the
caller's own structured input, consistent with how Notion's API itself expects a properties
object, not a broadened or narrowed schema. Provider errors are surfaced via
`r.body?.message` (Notion's own real error field) or a JSON fallback, never a raw stack trace
or credential value.

### SYNC / WEBHOOKS

Not applicable — no bidirectional sync system exists or was built for Notion; each action is
a direct, synchronous request/response call, consistent with the Gmail/Drive pattern this
mission reused. No Notion webhook exists in this repository's scope; none was invented.

### RELIABILITY

Notion execution reuses `execute()`'s existing retry infrastructure unchanged (`_withRetry`,
2 retries for non-high-risk actions, 0 for `delete_page`) and existing rate-limit checks
(`_checkRate`, using `TOOL_DEFS.notion.actions`' pre-existing `rateLimit` values) — no new
retry framework was created.

### WRITE SAFETY / IDEMPOTENCY

`create_page` calls Notion's real `POST /pages` once per invocation with no idempotency key —
consistent with `gdrive`'s `upload_file` (also a single real POST, no dedup key), matching
this file's existing convention rather than introducing an inconsistent new pattern.
`delete_page`'s archive-not-delete semantics make a duplicate call harmless (archiving an
already-archived page is a safe no-op on Notion's side, not a compounding destructive
action).

### ERROR HANDLING / OBSERVABILITY

Every new Notion action surfaces the real HTTP status and Notion's own error message
(`r.body?.message`) on failure, matching the exact shape every other real adapter in this
file already uses (Gmail: `r.body?.error?.message`; Drive: same). No credential or OAuth
token is logged — `_sanitizeParams()` (pre-existing, unmodified) already redacts any
token/secret/key-shaped parameter key before usage logging, applying uniformly to the new
Notion case with no special-casing needed.

### THE REAL DEFECT DISCOVERED WHILE BUILDING — a pre-existing, cross-cutting timeout gap

While writing the test for Jira's real-network-call assertion (against a deliberately
nonexistent Atlassian host), a genuine, pre-existing, cross-cutting reliability gap was found
live: `toolExecutionLayer.cjs`'s `_httpJson()` — the single shared HTTP function all real
tools in this file use (34 call sites: GitHub, Slack, Telegram, OpenRouter, Notion, Gmail,
GDrive, and now Jira/Linear) — **had no timeout at all**. A single call against an
unresponsive/non-resolving host hung for over a minute on the underlying connection attempt
before the OS-level timeout eventually surfaced a (very slow) rejection — confirmed by direct
measurement (one call alone spanned ~64 seconds). This is exactly the "no obvious timeout
gap" the mission's own quality gate calls out, affecting every existing tool in this file, not
just the 2 new ones added this pass. Fixed at the shared choke point (a 15-second default,
matching `storageService.cjs`'s own already-hardened timeout convention) rather than
per-tool, closing the gap for all 34 call sites at once — the correct minimal fix, not scope
creep, since it required touching only the one shared function.

### THE KEY FINDING — why this category could not be safely completed the way Notion/Jira/Linear were

Every provider genuinely completed in the prior 3 categories (Notion, Jira, Linear) shared
one property: the necessary credential or OAuth scope **already existed and was already
sufficient** for the missing execution — completing them meant only writing HTTP calls
against an already-granted permission. Google Calendar and Microsoft Calendar do not share
this property: neither the `google` nor `microsoft` OAuth provider entry requests any
calendar-scoped permission at all. Building real calendar execution now would require
**expanding the scope list on an already-live, already-used OAuth provider** — `getAuthUrl()`
does support an optional per-call scope override (confirmed by reading it directly), so the
architecture is not incapable of this, but changing what a shared, already-connected
provider's default consent requests is a decision with real operational consequences (any
user who already connected their Google/Microsoft account for Gmail/Drive/identity would need
to re-authorize to grant the new calendar permission) — a genuine product/architecture
decision, not a code-completeness gap this pass can safely resolve unilaterally. This is
categorically different from adding a `TOOL_DEFS` entry to an unused corner of an
already-sufficient grant.

### CLASSIFICATION

| Item | Classification |
|---|---|
| Google Calendar | PROBE-ONLY → **DECISION REQUIRED** to build real execution (requires an OAuth scope expansion on the live `google` provider) |
| Google Meet | ARCHITECTURE-ONLY → same **DECISION REQUIRED** gate (entirely dependent on Calendar) |
| Microsoft Calendar | NOT IN CURRENT SCOPE → same **DECISION REQUIRED** gate if ever built (requires an OAuth scope expansion on the live `microsoft` provider) |
| Zoom | NOT IN CURRENT SCOPE — zero footprint, no OAuth complexity even applicable |
| Internal content/community calendars | Confirmed unrelated, correctly not conflated with this category |

### DECISION REQUIRED

Two related decisions, not actioned unilaterally:

1. **Google Calendar/Meet.** If a future mission is explicitly asked to build this, the
   correct integration point is: add `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events` (or
   the narrower `calendar.events.readonly` if read-only is sufficient) to the `google`
   provider's `defaultScopes` in `oauthIntegrationLayer.cjs`, following the exact
   `_googleToken()` pattern already established for Gmail/Drive in `toolExecutionLayer.cjs`
   (reusing the same OAuth connection, not a second Google auth layer), then add a
   `TOOL_DEFS.gcalendar` entry and real `calendar.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/...` execution
   cases (list/read/create/update/cancel event) following the exact shape already proven for
   Notion/Gmail/Drive. Google Meet creation would then follow naturally by setting
   `conferenceData` on a created Calendar event (Google's own documented mechanism) — no
   separate Meet-specific OAuth or execution path is needed once Calendar exists. The
   consequence to weigh: existing connected Google accounts would need to re-consent to gain
   the new scope, since OAuth grants are not retroactively expandable without a new
   authorization round-trip.
2. **Microsoft Calendar.** Same reasoning: would require adding `Calendars.Read`/
   `Calendars.ReadWrite` to the `microsoft` provider's `defaultScopes`, then real
   `graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/events` execution cases, with the same re-consent
   consequence for any already-connected Microsoft account.

Neither was built this pass — no repository evidence shows either scope expansion has
already been decided, and doing so unilaterally would affect real, already-connected user
accounts' consent state, which is exactly the kind of decision this mission's own rules
reserve for explicit, deliberate authorization rather than an inferred default.

### Discovery — Internal Search / Analytics / BI

Three genuinely distinct, real, already-working internal capabilities were found and

- **Engineering code search** (`largeContextCodeSearch.cjs`) — real, live-mounted

- **Business/marketplace search** (`marketplaceService.search`) — real but simplistic

- **Agent-memory semantic search** (`semanticMemorySearch.cjs`) — genuinely real, executing

  `pgvector`/`faiss`/real embedding-API call exists anywhere), live-mounted at
  `/p26/memory/*`. Scoped to agent/engineering memory (failures/successes/decisions/
  knowledge), not customer/business/BI data. **This is where the category's one genuine,
  serious defect was found — see below.**
- **`data_analytics` department** (`departmentTemplateRegistry.cjs`) — investigated closely
  because, unlike every sibling department found in prior categories (Logistics, Accounting,
  Support, HR), it has **no self-documenting `note` field** at all. Verified this is
  correctly the *absence* of a needed caveat, not a documentation gap: its two skills,
  `analytics` and `revenue` (`skillRegistry.cjs`), have their own dedicated
  `executionHandler`s (`"analytics"`, `"revenue"`) and `source: "agentRegistry"` — **not**
  the generic `executionHandler: "ai"` / `source: "capability-buildout"` shape every
  honestly-labeled analysis-only skill in prior categories had. Traced the real dispatch
  chain (`executionEngine.cjs` → `agentRegistry.cjs` → `agents/business/analyticsAgent.cjs`/
  `agents/business/revenueAgent.cjs`) and confirmed both handlers are real data-aggregation
  code — reading `data/analytics.json`/`data/subscriptions.json`/`data/leads.json` directly
  and computing real conversion rates/revenue totals via arithmetic, zero LLM calls anywhere
  in either handler. **No note is needed because there is no analysis-only caveat to make —
  this department is genuinely `CODE-COMPLETE`, and adding a note would be inventing
  unnecessary text, not fixing anything.**

### THE REAL DEFECT FOUND — a live, exploitable cross-tenant search AND write vulnerability

Per this category's own explicit top-priority instruction ("BI/Search has a HIGH cross-tenant
data risk... check aggregation paths separately from document paths... check autocomplete/
facet paths separately"), `semanticMemorySearch.cjs` was audited specifically for tenant
isolation and a genuine, live, serious defect was found: **`orgId` was never threaded through
this file at all** — not on save, not on any of its 6 read/write functions — despite
`memoryPersistenceLayer.cjs` (the underlying store this file reads from) already having a
real, tested `orgId` filter mechanism (the "M-4" fix, already proven for other callers in
this same repo).

**Concrete, confirmed live effect (pre-fix):**
- `POST /p26/memory/search` extracted a client-supplied `projectId` from the request body but
  never resolved or passed `orgId` at all — `semanticSearch()` called
  `mpl.list({ limit: 5000 })` unscoped, meaning any authenticated user's search read across
  **every org's** stored memory nodes (failures, successes, decisions — potentially sensitive
  operational/business context) platform-wide, narrowing only by an optional, client-supplied
  `projectId` tag that is not a real authorization boundary.
- `crossProjectSearch()` was, by its own design and doc-comment, explicitly built to scan
  "ALL projectIds" with **no org-scoping option in its signature at all** — the worst
  instance of the pattern.
- `getKnowledgeGraph()` had the identical unscoped fetch, meaning the returned similarity
  graph's nodes and edges could span every tenant's memory.
- **`evolveKnowledge()` — reachable via `POST /p26/memory/evolve` — is a real WRITE path**
  (calls `mpl.update()` on qualifying nodes; `dryRun` defaults to `false`), meaning any
  authenticated user could mutate `importance`/`confidence` metadata on every org's memory
  nodes platform-wide, not just their own. This is the most serious instance, since it is a
  write, not a read.
- `phase26.js`'s router had no `attachOrg` middleware at all — only `requireAuth` — so there
  was no server-side org context available to any D2 handler even if the service functions
  had supported one.

This is exactly the repeated defect class this repo's own CLAUDE.md §6 identifies as its
single most-repeated real security issue, applied here to a subsystem (agent/engineering
memory) that had apparently never been assessed for multi-tenancy at all, unlike its own
underlying storage layer.

| Internal agent-memory semantic search (`semanticMemorySearch.cjs`) | EXISTS + INCOMPLETE → **fixed this pass** (live cross-tenant search AND write vulnerability closed) → now CODE-COMPLETE |
| `data_analytics` department (`analytics`/`revenue` skills) | CODE-COMPLETE (already, verified — real data aggregation, no LLM involved, no note needed) |

### DECISION REQUIRED

None. This category presented no architecture/product decision — the one real defect found
was safely, narrowly fixable within existing, already-proven architecture (reusing
`memoryPersistenceLayer.cjs`'s own already-tested `orgId` filter and the same `attachOrg`
middleware pattern used across dozens of other routes in this repo), and every external
provider is correctly zero-footprint with nothing to decide.

### CHANGES MADE

1. **`backend/services/semanticMemorySearch.cjs`**:
   - `saveTypedMemory(type, data, opts)` now stamps `opts.orgId` onto the saved node
     (additive, optional — legacy orgId-less nodes and non-org callers are unaffected).
   - `semanticSearch(query, opts)` now accepts `opts.orgId` and passes it to
     `mpl.list({ ..., orgId })` — reusing the existing, already-tested filter, not a second
     mechanism.
   - `searchFailures`/`searchSuccesses`/`searchDecisions` needed no code change — they
     already spread `...opts` through to `semanticSearch`, so they inherit the fix
     automatically.
   - `crossProjectSearch(query, opts)` now accepts and applies `opts.orgId` — its own
     doc-comment was corrected to state it spans all projects **within** a tenant, never
     across tenants.
   - `getKnowledgeGraph(opts)` now accepts and applies `opts.orgId`.
   - `evolveKnowledge(opts)` — the write path — now accepts and applies `opts.orgId`, so a
     scoped call can only ever fetch (and therefore only ever mutate via `mpl.update()`) its
     own org's nodes.
2. **`backend/routes/phase26.js`**:
   - Added `attachOrg` middleware (non-blocking, resolves `req.org` via the same
     server-side precedence — path param, then `X-Org-Id` header, never trusted blindly —
     every other org-scoped route in this repo already uses) to the `/p26` router. D1/D3/D4/D5
     routes in the same file are unaffected since they never read `req.org`.
   - Every D2 semantic-memory route now passes `orgId: req.org?.id || null` into its
     `semanticMemorySearch.cjs` call. Critically, `POST /p26/memory/typed`'s `safeOpts` spreads
     the client's own `req.body.opts` **first**, then overwrites `orgId` with the
     server-resolved value **last** — a client can never smuggle a different `orgId` through
     the request body, matching this repo's existing "never trust client-supplied tenant
     identifiers" rule everywhere else.

   unaffected.

authorization concept introduced. `orgId` is always server-resolved, never trusted from a
client-supplied body/query value, matching the confused-deputy fix already documented in
`orgMiddleware.cjs`'s own `attachOrg` (Phase B.7).

Developer API's actual package/service name) in any `.js`/`.cjs`/`.dart` file. `mobile/BUILD.md`

`androidpublisher` automation)... OUT OF SCOPE," "zero prior reference anywhere in the

### Apple App Store / App Store Connect

**ZERO FOOTPRINT.** No App Store Connect API code exists anywhere — zero references to
`app-store-connect-api`, `fastlane` (the one `.gitignore` hit is React Native's stock
boilerplate entry, not actual Fastlane usage, confirmed by direct inspection), `altool`,

does not mean release capability" conflation this category's own brief warns against.
Notarization exists only as part of the **Electron desktop app's macOS packaging** (via

upload code exists anywhere.

### Windows Signing / Distribution

**BUILD PIPELINE ONLY** — genuinely real, already well-built, and already correctly fixed
for its one known prior defect; no gap found requiring this pass's intervention.
`package.json`'s electron-builder config defines a real `win` target (`nsis`, x64). Real,
functional Authenticode signing plumbing exists in `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s
`desktop` job: `WIN_CSC_LINK`/`WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` (and the macOS equivalents
`CSC_LINK`/`CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`/`APPLE_ID`/`APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`/`APPLE_TEAM_ID`) are
read from GitHub Secrets and passed to `electron-builder --publish always` — these are
electron-builder's own real, correct environment variable names, not fabricated integration.
`docs/ELECTRON_SIGNING.md` (read in full) honestly and precisely documents: absent these 7
secrets, `npm run dist:*` "produces a real, working, **unsigned** build" — expected, safe
behavior for local development, with exact instructions for what a future operator would add
to activate real signing (no code change needed). **A real prior defect was already found and
fixed by an earlier mission** (Mission 53's finding, remediated by Mission 58, both already
present and unchanged): electron-builder's own documented behavior lets an unset
`CSC_LINK`/`WIN_CSC_LINK` silently produce an unsigned build with **zero warning** — a real
tagged release could ship unsigned with no visible signal. The already-existing fix
(`release.yml`'s "Verify code-signing status (warn-only)" step) makes this visible in the CI
log via each platform's own pre-installed verification tool (`codesign`/
`Get-AuthenticodeSignature`) without introducing a new dependency, and is deliberately
warn-only rather than a hard failure — this repo's own documented design treats signing as
genuinely optional/opt-in (matching `mobile/BUILD.md`'s equally opt-in-via-env-var shape for
Android), so the fix closes the *silent* part of the gap without forcing a build failure over
a legitimate, deliberate choice. Re-ran this pass: `tests/security/33-electron-navigation-signing-scope.cjs`
— **15/15 pass**, confirming this fix is intact and unmodified.

### Release Safety / Trigger Verification

Verified directly, per this category's top-priority "production release must NOT be silently
auto-approved" concern: `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s only trigger is
`on: push: tags: 'v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*'` — a deliberate, explicit human action (pushing a
semantic-version tag), never triggered by an ordinary push to `main` or any other automatic
event. The only real "publish" target that exists at all in this repository is GitHub
Releases for the desktop Electron app (mac/win/linux via `electron-builder --publish
always`) — there is no Play Store or App Store publish job in any workflow, so there is no
mobile-store auto-publish path to gate in the first place.
